task: Cycle 2: exact arbitrary-mean vector-feature rounding on a disjoint union of K2,2 blocks, with exact marginals, atomwise discrepancy, explicit support, and full bit/oracle costs.

source_snapshot.catalogue_scope: source-reported 722 manuscripts and 372 result families; not proof certification

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For r,k>=1, rational p in [0,1]^r, and explicit rational V=[v_1 ... v_r] in Q^{k x r} with ||v_i||_2<=1, assuming Li arXiv:2609.30044v1 Theorem 1.1, there is a deterministic polynomial-bit construction of a rational law D on z in {0,1}^r with at most r+1 atoms, E_D[z]=p, and max_{z in supp(D)} ||V(z-p)||_infinity<99.5. The construction uses T=ceil(log2(2r)) dyadic initialization, signed dyadic coarsening, and exact rational affine compression. In the disjoint-union-of-K2,2 encoding with edge features +/-v_i/2, every supported matching atom has discrepancy strictly below 199 and all actual-edge marginals equal the supplied p_i or 1-p_i.
claims.proof_path: SUPPORT_COMPRESSION_AUDIT.md, sections 'Synchronous residual cycle phase', 'Synchronous dyadic coarsening', 'Exact compression and bit-height proof', and 'K2,2 vector-block corollary'; base transition details in CYCLE2_REPORT.md, sections 'Initial residual b-matching cycle rounder' and 'Odd-numerator cycle coarsening'
claims.novelty_boundary: The deterministic <99 signing and rational bit-complexity are Li's source-reported theorem. Dyadic arbitrary-mean rounding is in the classical linear-discrepancy tradition, while Gram-Schmidt Walk already gives exact-mean sub-Gaussian laws. This report claims only the stated finite construction as an internally proved consequence and makes no novelty or priority claim.
claims.costs: Input is explicit rational p,V of total bit length L. Norm/marginal validation is exact polynomial time. The K2,2 specialization uses at most r synchronous initial residual rounds and T coarsening levels, at most r+1 active atoms and 2(r+1) candidates per round, and at most r+1 exact affine-dependence eliminations per compression in block-coordinate dimension r; these are proof-specified, not coded. There are at most (r+1)T Li signing calls, each on a k-by-s rational submatrix, s<=r. Li reports O(s^2 log(s+2)) updates, O(ks+s^(omega+2)log^3(s+2)) real-RAM arithmetic/comparisons, and polynomial bit complexity for rational input. The conservative common-weight-denominator bound from SUPPORT_COMPRESSION_AUDIT.md, with m=4r, is polynomial in (r,L,T); construction is deterministic and conditional on the Li theorem. No graph/count/separation oracle is used. Sampling the returned rational law by exact rejection takes expected O(log D) fair bits for common denominator D, with no finite worst-case bound. Algorithmic failure probability is zero conditional on the signing theorem.
claims.falsifier: A dyadic branch leaving [0,1]^r, changing the exact barycenter, or adding feature error at least 99*2^-t; an affine-dependence elimination that introduces a noncandidate atom or loses barycenter p; failure of the source signing theorem's promise on a rational submatrix; or an output edge marginal differing from p_i or 1-p_i.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof review of the Li signing implementation and an exact rational prototype of the support-compression pipeline; retain source-reported status until such review.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: Bansal-Dadush-Garg-Lovett's Gram-Schmidt Walk takes unit Euclidean vectors and arbitrary x0 in [-1,1]^r, returns x in {-1,1}^r with exact coordinate means because each randomized walk update is mean-zero, and gives sub-Gaussian vector discrepancy parameter sqrt(40); the paper reports O(r(r+k)^omega) runtime. This does not imply a deterministic bound on every supported atom.
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, section 'Strong matched prior art and novelty boundary'
claims.novelty_boundary: This is the strongest adjacent arbitrary-mean distributional discrepancy baseline found. Its sub-Gaussian tails are not an all-atoms bound; conditioning to a good event generally changes means. The paper does not state the exact rational bit-cost interface charged by the cycle-2 construction.
claims.costs: Source-reported O(r(r+k)^omega) arithmetic/runtime, with one linear system solve per walk step; exact fair-bit and rational-input bit bounds were not established in this audit.
claims.falsifier: The primary theorem's arbitrary-x0 interface, mean-zero step, or sqrt(40) sub-Gaussian guarantee being misstated; none was contradicted in the inspected theorem and algorithm ranges.
claims.next_gate: Compare both samplers on the same explicit rational input and cost model if an implementation comparison is needed.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: The pinned result-113 general-graph PM FPRAS and its self-reduction sampler target simple unweighted graph counts and TV-approximate uniform sampling. They do not supply arbitrary rational edge marginals or an all-support feature discrepancy bound. On disjoint K2,2 blocks the direct uniform law only gives p_i=1/2; a TV error also cannot guarantee exact marginals or eliminate every bad atom.
claims.proof_path: CYCLE2_REPORT.md, section 'Strong matched prior art and novelty boundary'; cycle-1 quantum_free_count_sample/FINAL_REPORT.md
claims.novelty_boundary: No claim is made against possible weighted gadget reductions; the pinned theorem does not provide one and the sampler mechanism is unnecessary for the present explicit block encoding.
claims.costs: The K2,2 law construction has no matching-count, feasibility, separation, or optimization oracle calls.
claims.falsifier: A theorem in the pinned source that accepts arbitrary supplied activities/marginals and guarantees atomwise feature bounds would change the scope verdict; the inspected source interface does not.
claims.next_gate: None for this construction; keep the release sampler as a negative control only.
